title.narrative: Increased capacity of Member States to develop and implement comprehensive employment policy frameworks

description.narrative: Increasing the capacity of Member States to develop and implement comprehensive employment policy frameworks is critical to fostering a human-centred recovery and structural transformation. The expected results include not only the development and application of these policies but also their integration into broader economic plans which will foster sustainable development, in line with SDG 8 and the objectives of ILO Convention 122. The final beneficiaries are economies and labour force worldwide, particularly those in sectors poised for growth such as the green, digital, and care economies. Institutions benefiting include national governments, employer organizations and workforce. The following are the major global deliverables and activities of the ILO in this policy area. (1) New research, including on: implementation and financing of employment policies; the role of employment policies in supporting multiple just transitions; coherence between pro-employment macroeconomic and industrial policies; the link between productivity and decent employment; trade and investment; decent work opportunities in the digital economy; and inequalities in the labour market (2) Improved policy advice, guidance tools and other knowledge products relevant to different stages of the employment policy cycle, including on the green, digital and care economies (3) Enhanced institutional capacity of constituents through training and peer learning in cooperation with the Turin Centre, including on diagnostics and employment impact assessments, policy design, implementation and financing (4) Support to the Implementation Strategy of the Global Accelerator on Jobs and Social Protection for Just Transitions (5) Partnerships and advocacy for the promotion of Convention122, Recommendation 204, and Recommendation 205 The strategy is carried out through partnerships mainly with ILO constituents and international bodies.
